transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’m here because… I’ve been hearing things at work. Voices, mostly, coming through the call-light speaker or the vents in the hall. They sound real—like someone right next to me—saying which patient records were changed. But when I look around, it’s quiet, and nobody else seems to hear it.
Can you tell me if the voices you hear seem to come from inside your head or from outside, like through the speaker or vent?

Outside. It’s not like a thought in my head. It sounds like it’s coming through the call-light speaker or the vents… clear, like someone’s right there talking about which records got changed. Nobody else seems to hear it, though.
Have you noticed any other strange or unusual things happening that others don't seem to notice, or do you believe something that others might find hard to understand?

I mean… I don’t know if it sounds strange, but the wound-care charts have a pattern. It’s not just late entries or coding mistakes like my supervisor says.

I caught it, and now I can tell they’re watching what I write. They don’t want anyone seeing it.

When you say 'they’re watching what you write' and 'they don’t want anyone seeing it,' can you tell me more about who you believe 'they' are and if you feel like you're being followed or spied on in other situations?

I don’t really know who all of them are. Management, I guess… people who handle the charts. They know I noticed the pattern in the wound-care records, and now it feels like they’re paying attention to what I write because I’m the one who caught it.

I’m not saying I see someone following me around everywhere. It’s more… at work, with the records. They don’t want it seen.
Do you ever feel like your thoughts are being put into your mind by someone else, taken out, or that others can know what you're thinking without you saying it?

I don’t know about thoughts being put in or taken out. It’s more… the charts. I know there’s a pattern in the wound-care records, and they don’t want it seen. Even when my supervisor says it’s just late entries or coding errors, I can tell they’re watching what I write because I’m the one who caught it.
Outside of work, do you ever feel like someone is trying to hide information from you or that there are patterns or meanings in everyday events that others don’t seem to notice?

Not really outside of work. It’s… mainly the wound-care charts. There’s a pattern there, and management doesn’t want it seen.

My supervisor keeps saying it’s late entries or coding mistakes, but that’s not what it feels like. I can tell they’re watching what I write because I caught it.
Do you believe that the people watching your work are part of a larger group or organization that is involved in this in any way?
I don’t know if it’s some big organization. I just know management doesn’t want that pattern in the wound-care charts seen. And since I noticed it, it feels like they’re watching what I write.
Do you think management is coordinating with others or acting in a deliberate way to hide the pattern you noticed in the wound-care charts?

I think it’s deliberate, yes. I don’t know who all is involved, but those charts show something, and management doesn’t want people seeing it. My supervisor keeps calling it late entries or coding mistakes, but… I don’t buy that. They’ve been watching what I write since I caught it.
Do you think this effort by management to hide the pattern in the charts is part of something bigger, like a wider plan or conspiracy that goes beyond just your workplace?
I don’t know if I’d call it a wider conspiracy. I just know the charts show a pattern, and management doesn’t want anyone seeing it. And since I caught it, they’ve been watching what I write.
Do you believe that anyone outside of your workplace, like government agencies or other organizations, is involved in trying to hide the pattern you noticed in the wound-care charts?

I don’t know about government agencies or anything like that. I just know the charts show something management doesn’t want seen. My supervisor keeps saying it’s late entries or coding mistakes, but since I caught it, I can tell they’ve been watching what I write.
Even though you mentioned this mainly happens at work, have you ever felt that what you do or write outside of work might also be watched or monitored because of what you've noticed in the charts?

Maybe… not everywhere, I don’t know. It’s mostly work. But since I found that pattern in the wound-care charts, I’m more careful about what I write. My supervisor keeps saying it’s just late entries or coding errors, but I can tell they’re watching what I put down because I’m the one who caught it.
Do you feel that the voices you hear about the patient records are connected to your belief that management is watching what you write about the wound-care charts?

Yes… I think so. The voices are about the records, about which ones were changed. I hear them from the call-light speaker or the hallway vents, clear like someone standing right there, even when it’s quiet. Nobody else seems to hear it.
Do you think the voices you hear and the feeling of being watched at work are part of a larger plan that might involve people or forces beyond just your workplace management?

I don’t know about… larger forces. I just know the charts show a pattern they don’t want people seeing. My supervisor keeps saying it’s late entries or coding mistakes, but it doesn’t feel like that. They watch what I write because I caught it.
Do you think that the voices you hear or the feeling of being watched at work are meant to specifically target or harm you, or are they just part of how things are being handled at work?

I don’t know if I’d say they’re trying to harm me exactly. It’s more… they don’t want me putting down what I found. The wound-care charts show a pattern, and my supervisor keeps saying it’s just late entries or coding mistakes, but I know what I saw. They’re watching what I write because I’m the one who caught it.
Have you ever believed something strongly that others found hard to understand or accept, even when there was no evidence to support it, outside of your concerns about the wound-care charts at work?

Not really outside of that… it’s mostly the charts. I know what I saw in those wound-care records. My supervisor says it’s just late entries or coding mistakes, but it doesn’t feel like that. I can tell they’re watching what I write because I’m the one who noticed it.
Do you ever have these kinds of beliefs or feelings about things being hidden or watched in areas of your life outside of work, like with family, friends, or other activities?

Not really… not with my family or anything. It’s mostly at work. The charts, the wound-care ones, they show something, and management doesn’t want it seen. My supervisor keeps saying it’s late entries or coding mistakes, but I know what I caught. They watch what I write because of that.
Outside of work, have you ever had a strong belief that something was being hidden from you or that you were being watched, even if others didn’t share that belief?

Not really outside of work. It’s… it’s the same thing I’ve been saying. The wound-care charts show a pattern, and management doesn’t want people seeing it. My supervisor can call it late entries or coding mistakes, but I know what I saw. And I can tell they’re watching what I write because I’m the one who caught it.
Have you ever had any beliefs that others don’t share or that seem unusual, even when there’s no clear reason for them, in any part of your life, even briefly?

I mean… only what I already said. The wound-care charts. I know there’s a pattern there that management doesn’t want seen. My supervisor keeps saying it’s just late entries or coding mistakes, but… I can tell they’re watching what I write because I’m the one who caught it.

Have you ever had any unusual beliefs or suspicions about things happening in your life that others might not understand, even if you didn't have proof, and that were not related to your concerns at work?

No… not outside of that. I mean, the thing with the charts is what I’m talking about. I don’t have some other… beliefs like that in my personal life. It’s the wound-care records. There’s something there, and they don’t want it seen. That’s why they watch what I write.

target_item.manifestation: I know the wound-care charts are showing a pattern management doesn't want anyone to see, and even when my supervisor says it's just late entries or coding mistakes, I can tell they're watching what I write because I'm the one who caught it.
target_item.reason: The question is directly asking about unusual beliefs or suspicions held without proof, which corresponds to delusions; it is specifically probing whether they occur outside work.

patient.answer: No… not outside of that. I mean, the thing with the charts is what I’m talking about. I don’t have some other… beliefs like that in my personal life. It’s the wound-care records. There’s something there, and they don’t want it seen. That’s why they watch what I write.

inference.note: This turn supports the presence of delusional beliefs primarily in the context of work (e.g., belief in a hidden pattern in wound-care charts and being watched because of it), which aligns with delusional disorder. There is no clear evidence of hallucinations independent of the delusional context, ruling out schizophrenia spectrum disorders (F23.x). The delusions appear non-bizarre and circumscribed, without generalized oddness, negative symptoms, or disorganization, reducing the likelihood of F23.0 (Acute polymorphic psychotic disorder), F23.8 (Other acute psychotic disorders), and F23.9 (Acute psychotic disorder, unspecified).

opening_question.intent: Greet the patient and obtain the chief complaint or reason for the visit
opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with persistent, non-bizarre delusions centered around a specific theme (i.e., belief that management is deliberately concealing a pattern in wound-care records and monitoring their documentation). The delusional system is circumscribed and focused on this theme without broader psychotic features or disorganization. No evidence of mood episodes, substance use, or pervasive delusional themes that would suggest an alternative diagnosis.
